content.user_title: Model ABS Cash Flows and Stress Scenarios
content.value_statement: Data-asset ABS structures need defensible cash-flow assumptions and visible downside protection. This skill guides coverage analysis, stress testing, sensitivity review, tranching, and credit enhancement.
actual_capabilities: Assesses whether cash flows are identifiable, measurable, transferable, and predictable.
Calculates period coverage ratios and identifies the weakest payment period.
Runs baseline, 20 percent downside, and 50 percent downside scenarios.
Analyzes churn, pricing, combined shocks, concentration, and threshold breakpoints.
Estimates senior, mezzanine, and junior tranche proportions with enhancement options.
Defines model assumptions, review checks, deliverables, and monitoring triggers.
limitations: It does not include an executable spreadsheet or the referenced external stress-testing tool.
Results depend on complete contracts, payment schedules, historical cash flows, and recovery assumptions.
Coverage and tranche ranges are experience-based references, not mandatory regulatory thresholds.
Outputs do not replace advice from rating agencies, counsel, auditors, arrangers, or regulators.

use_cases.title: Screen a data-asset pool
use_cases.description: Test cash-flow eligibility and identify missing evidence before detailed ABS modeling begins.

use_cases.title: Challenge downside resilience
use_cases.description: Compare coverage under revenue, churn, pricing, and customer concentration shocks.

use_cases.title: Prepare a structure proposal
use_cases.description: Estimate tranche proportions and enhancement levels for discussion with transaction advisers.

prompt_templates.title: Check modeling readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this asset pool for identifiable, measurable, transferable, and predictable cash flows. List missing evidence and state whether modeling should proceed.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner screening before building a model

prompt_templates.title: Calculate coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Using my periodic net cash flows and debt-service schedule, calculate each coverage ratio. Identify the weakest period and explain the result.

prompt_templates.title: Run stress and sensitivity tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Run baseline, 20 percent downside, and 50 percent downside scenarios. Test churn and pricing separately and together, then identify threshold breakpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Design tranche and enhancement options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare three senior and junior tranche structures for my target rating. Quantify overcollateralization, cash-flow coverage, excess spread, and residual risks.

output_examples.input: The pool has 24 monthly observations, signed contracts, and traceable invoices. Review modeling readiness.
output_examples.output: Readiness: conditional pass. Identification, measurement, and predictability are supported. Confirm transfer rights and remove disputed or related-party receipts before modeling.

output_examples.input: Baseline minimum coverage is 1.28. Revenue falls by 20 percent and 50 percent.
output_examples.output: Baseline coverage clears the 1.20 reference. The stressed minima are 1.02 and 0.64. Severe stress requires explicit liquidity or payment support.

output_examples.input: Propose a structure for a concentrated pool targeting stronger senior protection.
output_examples.output: Start with a smaller senior tranche, at least 20 percent junior support, and measurable overcollateralization. Add a largest-customer-loss test before finalizing.

best_practices: Reconcile every modeled cash flow to contracts, invoices, ledgers, and collection records.
Apply one documented assumption set across baseline, stress, sensitivity, and structure tests.
Report the weakest payment period, assumption sources, breakpoints, and unresolved data gaps.
anti_patterns: Do not forecast growth above historical evidence without a documented and testable basis.
Do not use average coverage when one payment period has a material shortfall.
Do not present reference ratios as guaranteed ratings or regulatory approval.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide periodic collections, contracts, invoices, customer concentration, defaults, recoveries, payment dates, fees, and the proposed debt-service schedule.

faq.question: Can this skill create an executable financial model?
faq.answer: It can define calculations and analyze supplied data, but the package contains no executable spreadsheet or modeling program.

faq.question: Which stress scenarios are included?
faq.answer: The playbook uses baseline, 20 percent downside, and 50 percent downside scenarios, plus churn, pricing, and customer concentration tests.

faq.question: Does a 1.20 coverage ratio guarantee issuance?
faq.answer: No. It is a reference threshold. Asset quality, legal structure, ratings, enhancement, disclosures, and regulatory review still determine feasibility.

faq.question: How does the skill address concentrated customers?
faq.answer: It recommends reporting the top three customers and testing the complete loss of a major customer.

faq.question: Can the output replace professional opinions?
faq.answer: No. Rating agencies, counsel, auditors, arrangers, and regulators must review conclusions within their responsibilities.
